vocabulary.meaning: a strong and difficult-to-control need to do or use something
examples: Screen addiction can affect sleep and concentration.
Some people describe their television habits as an addiction.

vocabulary.meaning: to watch many episodes of a programme one after another
examples: We binge-watched the whole series over the weekend.
Streaming platforms make it easy to binge-watch.

vocabulary.meaning: the amount of time spent using televisions, computers, or phones
examples: Parents often worry about children's screen time.
Reducing screen time before bed may improve sleep.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who watches television or online video
examples: The programme attracted millions of viewers.
Viewers can now choose what they watch and when.

vocabulary.meaning: involving a lot of sitting and little physical activity
examples: Watching television for hours is a sedentary activity.
A sedentary lifestyle can affect your health.

vocabulary.meaning: something you do regularly, often without thinking
examples: Watching the news after dinner became a daily habit.
Changing a long-term habit can be difficult.

vocabulary.meaning: activities or programmes designed to give people enjoyment
examples: Television remains a major form of entertainment.
People now have many more entertainment choices.

vocabulary.meaning: a small device used to operate a television from a distance
examples: He picked up the remote control and changed the channel.
The remote control was hidden under the sofa.
That programme has a very loyal audience.
She watches a documentary programme every week.

vocabulary.meaning: to stop a device from operating or to stop paying attention to something
examples: Try to switch off the television during meals.
Sometimes it is healthy to switch off and do something active.
